The Paper.js layer z-order contract, confirmed by reading source and by `git grep`: at the moment this scope's first packet finishes executing (before any user layer exists), `project.layers` bottom-to-top is stageLayer(361), onionPrevLayer(362), onionNextLayer(363), ghostAllLayer(364), arcLayer(366), nodeLayer(367), marqueeLayer(368), xformLayer(369) — each `new Layer()` call appends to the top of Paper's project layer stack in source declaration order, so xformLayer (declared last) is topmost of these eight. `createUserLayer` (app.js:377-387) does `arcLayer.activate();var l=new Layer(...);l.insertBelow(arcLayer);` (line 378) for every new user layer — `insertBelow` re-splices the new Layer to sit directly under arcLayer, which both (a) keeps every user-drawn layer permanently sandwiched BETWEEN the four background/onion layers (below) and the arc/node/marquee/xform UI-overlay trio (above), regardless of how many user layers exist, and (b) means the layer created/reinserted LAST ends up directly below arcLayer, i.e. visually on top of every OTHER user layer. `reorderLayersAtGap` (app.js:438-488) exploits exactly this: after splicing both `state.layers` and `userLayers` into the new order (lines 473-474), line 475 does `userLayers.forEach(function(l){l.insertBelow(arcLayer);});` — iterating index 0 first (temporarily placed directly below arcLayer) through index length-1 LAST (ending up directly below arcLayer, i.e. topmost of the user-layer stack) — so ascending array index order in `state.layers`/`userLayers` always corresponds to ascending Paper.js z-order, matching the function's own in-source comment (app.js:412-417, "ending with the highest index on top").
